recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. The current build inputs already communicate the distinction requested by FHIR-5780, and adding more prose would duplicate maintained datatype guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-5780 was Published/Persuasive and asked whether the FHIR id datatype definition was inconsistent because uuid is a URN containing colons while the id regex does not allow colons. The final Jira resolution was to add documentation explaining the intended distinction.
initial_application: Jira records the clarification as applied in SVN revision 4608, and git history contains 09b9e817 with the subject '#5780 - improved documentation about id vs uri'. The visible git-svn patch for that revision does not alter the current datatype text, but the requested clarification is present in the active datatype page and was preserved through later datatype refactors.
additional_context: FHIR-3768 added ISO 18232 context for id, and FHIR-3750 later finalized 64-character, case-sensitive, upper/lower ASCII id semantics with lowercase UUIDs. The combined branch already contains the FHIR-3750 fix that aligned source/datatypes/primitives.xml with those later semantics. FHIR-12889 concerns Element.id representation rather than removing the id datatype's value-form rule.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. source/datatypes.html already says a FHIR URL's last path segment is the id datatype and that a full UUID is a uri, not an id; source/datatypes/primitives.xml already allows an unprefixed OID or UUID pattern under the id regex.

related_jiras.note: Added ISO 18232 context and variance text for the id datatype, reinforcing that FHIR id is a constrained identifier form.
Later final decision changed id length/case rules and is already represented on the combined branch by commit 758b63c; it is compatible with this no-change audit.
Later id-related issue resolved Element.id representation rather than removing FHIR id's 64-character/value-form rule.
